maya: Hey team — running into weird score ranges from the /rerank endpoint. Some candidates are negative, others are large positive decimals. Do these map to probabilities or logits? How should we interpret them for thresholding and A/B rules?

jordan: Can you paste the request/response you used (sanitized)? quick take: sorting should be stable even if not normalized, but thresholding needs clarification.

maya: Sure — minimal repro:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-re-rank-v2","query":"best pizza","candidates":["pizza near me","best sushi","top pizzerias"],"top_k":3}'
```
Response snippet: 
```json
{"candidates":[{"text":"pizza near me","score":-3.1},{"text":"best sushi","score":0.002},{"text":"top pizzerias","score":4.7}]}
```
We expected something between 0-1, or at least comparable across requests. This is causing our rule that drops results with score < 0.5 to behave oddly.

eli: This matches a common confusion — rerank outputs can be raw logits depending on model/variant. Raw logits are unnormalized and can be negative. Sorting by score is correct, but absolute thresholds only make sense after converting to a probability-like scale.

chris: Quick options: (1) apply softmax across candidate set to get probabilities; (2) use logistic/softmax on pairwise score deltas if you have a base item; (3) if you need 0-1 comparators per item independently, min-max normalize per-request (watch out for tiny ranges).

maya: Thanks. Two follow-ups: (a) is the output always logits, or does it vary per model? (b) softmax across candidates — that's O(N) per request, fine — any recommended numeric stability tips?

jordan: a) It can vary by model/release — some model variants return calibrated scores (pseudo-probs) while others return uncalibrated scores. We should treat raw 'score' as model-defined. We'll check whether rwd-re-rank-v2 is returning logits. b) For softmax, subtract max(score) before exponentiating to avoid overflow: softmax_i = exp(score_i - max)/sum(exp(score_j - max)).

eli: Also note: temperature/scaling may differ. If you need consistent behavior across model rollouts, request a model contract from product specifying whether scores are logits, log-odds, or already normalized. For quick deploys, add an adapter that normalizes scores at the service boundary.

maya: Great — last thing: we saw one request where scores were all negative but ordering was correct. So as long as we sort descending, it's safe?

chris: Yes — ranking is ordinal. Negative-only arrays just mean the model's baseline is below 0 for those candidates. Use softmax if you need interpretable probabilities. If you rely on thresholds, choose them post-normalization and record which normalization method you use in feature flags.

maya: Sending model name + 10 sample requests to the support ticket now. Any other repro tips?

jordan: Include the full request payload, model name, timestamp, exact response JSON, and a small set of examples where thresholding failed. If you can, include a deterministic seed or request id so we can correlate in logs.

support-bot: Ticket created: #CS-3421 — assigned to eng-ml. (posted by @jordan)

maya: Thanks — will attach samples. :pray:

eli: One more note for docs team: add a short section in rerank docs explaining that scores may be raw logits and provide example softmax code. @chris can you add?

chris: Yep, I'll add a short snippet and guidance today. :memo:
